title: How heavy is each packet of rice?
description: A wholesale merchant packs one kilogram of rice into four packets of equal weight. The kilogram is cut into four equal parts, one for each packet, and the parts are put back together to check.
teaching_notes: One idea: one whole cut into some number of equal parts gives parts that are each one fractional unit. Watch for students who write four as the weight of each packet.

source: A wholesale merchant packed 1 kg of rice in four packets of equal weight. The weight of each packet is ____ kg.
video_script.why: The child cuts one kilogram into four equal parts, the way a roti is cut for four children, and names one part as a fraction.
video_script.substitution: Treat the one kilogram of rice as one roti shared equally among four children.
video_script.anchor: One kilogram of rice packed into four packets of equal weight
video_script.payoff_line: Each packet weighs one fourth of a kilogram
maths_rules: 1 kg packed in 4 packets of equal weight: cut 1 kg into 4 equal parts
one of 4 equal parts is 1/4, so each packet weighs 1/4 kg
check: 4 equal parts put together make the whole 1 kg again, and 4 x 1/4 = 1
video_script.design: One idea: one whole cut into four equal parts gives one fourth for each part. Same method as sharing one roti among four. The bar and the four packets stay on the board to the end.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a sack marked 1 kg of rice and, beside it, four empty packets in a row

marks.book: the title card From your book appears
marks.sack: a sack marked 1 kg of rice appears
marks.packets: four empty packets appear in a row beside it
marks.ask: the words weight of each packet appear

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about a wholesale merchant.
<bookmark mark='sack'/>The merchant has one kilogram of rice in a sack.
<bookmark mark='packets'/>He packs all of it into four packets of equal weight.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is the weight of each packet?

beats.on_screen: the sack and the packets hold still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: the sack becomes one long bar that stands for the whole kilogram; the four packets stand above it

marks.bar: the sack becomes one long bar that stands for the whole kilogram
marks.same: the four packets line up above the bar, all of equal weight

narration: <bookmark mark='bar'/>Think of the one kilogram as one whole, like one full roti.
<bookmark mark='same'/>The packets have equal weight, so each packet takes an equal share of the rice.

beats.on_screen: Given: 1 kg of rice packed in 4 packets of equal weight

marks.given: the one kilogram and the four packets are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, one kilogram of rice is packed in four packets of equal weight.

beats.on_screen: To find: the weight of each packet

marks.find: the words weight of each packet are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the weight of one single packet out of the four.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: 1 kg is shared equally by 4 packets

marks.share: an arrow joins the bar to the four packets

narration: <bookmark mark='share'/>Step one, share the one kilogram equally among the four packets. Do it the same way as the example in your book.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: cut the bar into 4 equal parts; one part for each packet

marks.cut: three cut lines split the bar into four equal parts
marks.one: one part lights up above one packet

narration: <bookmark mark='cut'/>Step two, cut the whole into four equal parts, because there are four packets.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Each packet takes one of those equal parts for its own weight.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: check, the 4 equal parts put together make the whole 1 kg again

marks.back: the four parts slide back together into the full bar

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step three, check. When we put the four equal parts together, they make the whole kilogram again.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Each packet weighs one fourth of a kilogram. One of four equal parts is one fourth.
